extDesc.message: Tab audio recorder: records the sound playing in a tab and saves it as an MP3 or WAV file.

waiting.message: Waiting for sound. Recording starts when audio plays and stops when the track ends or after 5 seconds of pause.

idle.message: Records audio of this tab only.

err_unsupported.message: This page can't be recorded (browser or add-on pages are not supported).

device_intro.message: Records everything that arrives on the chosen input: a microphone, a virtual cable, Stereo Mix. This lets you record sound that a tab does not hand over: send the system sound to a virtual device and choose it here. The file contains all sound of that device, not one tab.

device_silent.message: No signal from this device. Check that the system sound goes to it (see the help below).

device_err_open.message: Could not open the device. Check the microphone permission for Firefox in the system settings.

help_drivers.message: Virtual audio device drivers are not part of the extension: install them separately from the official sites, each has its own license.

help_mac1.message: Install the virtual device BlackHole 2ch (a separate program from its official site).

help_mac2.message: Open Audio MIDI Setup and create a Multi-Output Device: your speakers or headphones first, then BlackHole 2ch.

help_mac3.message: In the sound settings choose this device for output. Its volume cannot be changed with the keys: use the player or the speakers.

help_mac4.message: Choose BlackHole 2ch here and press Start recording: everything the computer plays goes into the file.

help_mac_perm.message: On first use macOS asks for microphone access for Firefox: allow it (virtual devices count as microphones). If you refused: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone.

help_mac_rate.message: If the recording crackles after a few minutes: in Audio MIDI Setup set the format of BlackHole 2ch to 44100 Hz (the same as your speakers or headphones). With a different sample rate Firefox resamples the sound on the fly and breaks it.

help_win1.message: Simplest option, if your sound driver has it: Stereo Mix (it may also be called "What U Hear" or "Wave Out Mix"). It is hidden by default: Win+R → mmsys.cpl → Recording tab → right-click empty space → Show Disabled Devices → right-click it → Enable. Then choose it here. It records everything the computer plays; on many computers its level follows the Windows volume (quiet volume gives a quiet file), and with headphones plugged in it may go silent.

help_win2.message: If there is no such device, or you want to record only Firefox at full level while you keep listening: install the virtual cable VB-CABLE from its official site and restart the computer.

help_win3.message: Send only Firefox into the cable. Windows 10: Settings → System → Sound → App volume and device preferences. Windows 11: Settings → System → Sound → Volume mixer. Next to Firefox set Output to CABLE Input (not CABLE In 16ch). Leave the main output device as it is: your speakers, headphones or TV. If Firefox is not in the list, play any sound in it first.

help_win4.message: Close Firefox completely and open it again: Windows applies the new output only to a freshly started Firefox.

help_win5.message: To keep hearing Firefox: Win+R → mmsys.cpl → Recording tab → CABLE Output → Properties → Listen tab → turn on Listen to this device and in Playback through this device choose Default Playback Device → OK. Then the sound follows whatever device is the main one at the moment: speakers, headphones or a TV over HDMI.

help_win6.message: Choose CABLE Output here and start recording. The level does not depend on the Windows volume. A slight delay in what you hear is normal.

help_win7.message: Silence and no signal here? Check the main output device in the sound settings: when a TV or monitor is connected over HDMI, Windows may make it the main one. Check that Firefox is still on CABLE Input (the choice can reset after an update) and that CABLE Input and CABLE Output have the same format (Properties → Advanced). To stop using the cable, set Firefox back to Default.

help_linux1.message: PipeWire and PulseAudio give every output a monitor named "Monitor of …". Choose it in the device list.

help_linux2.message: If there is no such item, start recording and in pavucontrol on the Recording tab choose "Monitor of …" for Firefox.

link_apple.message: Apple: playing audio through several devices

cmdRecord.message: Start / stop recording the current tab

cmdWatch.message: Start / cancel waiting for sound in the current tab

ignore_site_hint.message: Record at full level even if the site's player volume is turned down or the tab is muted. Off: sites that play through Web Audio are recorded as you hear them.

err_nosource.message: No track to download was found on this page. Start playing it, then try again.

err_mse.message: This player streams in a way that cannot be saved without playback yet. Use recording.

err_live.message: This is a live stream: it has no end, so it can only be recorded.

err_drm.message: The player plays a protected (DRM) version of the track and the page has no open version: it cannot be saved without playback. Try recording it with "Record from an audio device" (for example through BlackHole).

err_codec.message: This audio format cannot be decoded by Firefox, so the track cannot be saved without playback. Use recording.

fast_collect.message: Collecting the track as it loads:

fast_collect_now.message: press to save what is collected

warn_silent.message: The tab's sound does not reach the recording: the file will be silent. This happens with protected (DRM) audio and some players. Record through a virtual input: "Record from an audio device" (for example BlackHole).

warn_drm.message: The track is protected (DRM): recording the tab gives silence. Record through a virtual input: "Record from an audio device" (for example BlackHole).

cmdFast.message: Save the whole track now (no playback)

page_icon.message: Show the icon in the address bar

hotkeys_manual.message: Add-ons and themes → gear menu → Manage Extension Shortcuts
